email.body1:
Jordan, saw Placer.ai integrated its foot traffic data into Green Street's platform and keeps expanding into government and economic-development accounts.

For an SDR, that kind of expansion means more verticals and accounts to touch than you can follow up on, and response speed is where deals slip. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up on its own, so you cover more without new ramp: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I had our AI SDR draft three personalized emails to Placer's top three target accounts. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through them?
email.body2:
Jordan, quick follow-up for Placer.ai.

Most SDRs lose pipeline to slow follow-up and inconsistent sequencing as new verticals open up, not a lack of leads. Tightening that motion is usually the fastest lift you can show your manager this quarter.

Worth 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three specific changes I would make. Our best practices alone tend to lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Jordan, last bit of proof for Placer.ai.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how your reply rate likely compares to other data and analytics SDR teams. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jordan, I will stop reaching out on this one, but did not want to leave you empty-handed.

If speeding up follow-up across new verticals is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. A growing book keeps you plenty busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I will tailor it to Placer either way.
